raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Detector-side hardening for #27336 (auto-closed by inactivity; the earlier detector PR #27337 went stale). @JustinTong0323 on that issue: "Worth keeping both: the detector hardening as a safety net, and the grammar fix for the root cause." The grammar fix (mlc-ai/xgrammar#651) is still open. With `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` and `tool_choice="required"`, arguments come back with the close marker inside the value, e.g. `{"city": "Shanghai\n"}`; `` and a bare `` token; when it never appears, the value runs on to the next `` and the drifted marker stays inside the argument. Clients that validate arguments against the tool schema reject the call; clients that do not run the tool with a polluted string. The grammar-side fix lives in xgrammar. This PR is the detector-level safety net the issue asks for, so that a call which does complete yields a clean value. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py`: - One compiled regex, `malformed_parameter_end_regex = r"\s*)[^<>]*>?\s*$"`: a trailing ``, followed by non-bracket characters and an optional `>`. `[^<>]*` keeps it from eating tags that are legitimately part of the value. - `_clean_param_value(raw_value)`: strips one such trailer, then the existing newline trim. Both the non-streaming regex path and the streaming cursor path call it, so the two paths cannot diverge again. `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_qwen3_coder_detector.py` (new file; no unit test covered this detector): - non-streaming: three drifted markers, each yields `{"city": "Shanghai", "days": 3}` - streaming in 3-character chunks with a drifted marker: same result - well-formed ``: unchanged - angle brackets inside a value (`a tag city`): preserved The two drifted-marker cases fail on `main` with `{'city': 'Shanghai\n', ...}`, the reported symptom; the two guard cases pass on both, which is what shows the regex does not over-strip. **Related open PRs.** None of them handles drifted close markers, but some touch the same file. #38624 (phantom tool calls from quoted markup) also adds `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_qwen3_coder_detector.py`, and it and #36835 edit the streaming path near the hunk changed here; whichever lands first, I'll rebase and merge the test classes. #40741 / #40778 change the text after `` in `detect_and_parse`, not parameter values. Existing detector tests: `pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/` gives the same results with and without this change (the new file adds 4 passing tests; no previously passing test changes). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: no model forward change. Parser output for well-formed calls is byte-identical (guard tests). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: one anchored regex substitution per parameter value. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks (`pre-commit run --files ...` clean, including `validate registered test CI registries`). - [x] Add unit tests (`python test/registered/unit/function_call/test_qwen3_coder_detector.py`: 4 tests, 3 subtests; registered with `register_cpu_ci(1.0, "base-a-test-cpu")`). - [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing change). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (not applicable). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance (two-line comment anchored to the regex with the cross-boundary reference; regression docstring states the black-box constraint). Developed with AI assistance (Claude); every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run locally by me. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #41276458354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41276458354) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41276458241](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41276458241) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #41276458140](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41276458140)

nodes.body: Pushed a follow-up: the marker strip now only applies when the value wasn't closed by `</parameter>`, so a legitimate value ending in e.g. `</parameters>` is kept, and it finds the marker in linear time (the end-anchored regex was quadratic on long whitespace runs). Added tests for both.
@JustinTong0323 gentle ping when you have a moment. This is the detector-side safety net you suggested on #27336 ("worth keeping both"). Happy to adjust scope or naming.

@@ -41,9 +41,14 @@ def __init__(self):
             r"<function=(.*?)</function>|<function=(.*)$", re.DOTALL
         )
         self.tool_call_parameter_regex = re.compile(
-            r"<parameter=(.*?)(?:</parameter>|(?=<parameter=)|(?=</function>)|$)",
+            r"<parameter=(.*?)(</parameter>|(?=<parameter=)|(?=</function>)|$)",
             re.DOTALL,
         )
+        # Constrained decoding only locks the "</parameter" prefix, so a value may close
+        # with "</parameter1>" or a bare "</parameter"; drop once xgrammar#651 is fixed.
+        self.malformed_parameter_end_regex = re.compile(
+            r"</parameter(?!>)[^<>]*>?\s*", re.DOTALL
+        )
 
         # Streaming State
         # Base class already initializes _buffer, we just use it directly
@@ -95,6 +100,21 @@ def _get_arguments_config(
         logger.warning(f"Tool '{func_name}' is not defined in the tools list.")
         return {}, {}
 
+    def _clean_param_value(self, raw_value: str, closed: bool) -> str:
+        # Only a value that no real </parameter> closed can end in a drifted
+        # marker; a properly closed value may itself end in e.g. "</parameters>".
+        if not closed:
+            idx = raw_value.rfind("</parameter")
+            if idx != -1 and self.malformed_parameter_end_regex.fullmatch(
+                raw_value, idx
+            ):
+                raw_value = raw_value[:idx].rstrip()
+        if raw_value.startswith("\n"):
+            raw_value = raw_value[1:]
+        if raw_value.endswith("\n"):
+            raw_value = raw_value[:-1]
+        return raw_value
+
     def _get_param_type(self, param_schema: Any) -> str:
         """Infer the parser conversion type from a JSON schema parameter."""
         inferred_type = infer_type_from_json_schema(param_schema)

@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@ +"""Unit tests for Qwen3CoderDetector -- no server, no model loading.""" + +import json +import time + +from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool +from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen3_coder_detector import Qwen3CoderDetector +from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci +from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase + +register_cpu_ci(1.0, "base-a-test-cpu") + +TOOLS = [ + Tool( + type="function", + function=Function( + name="get_weather", + description="Get weather information", + parameters={ + "type": "object", + "properties": { + "city": {"type": "string"}, + "days": {"type": "integer"}, + }, + "required": ["city"], + }, + ), + ) +] + + +def _call(city_block: str) -> str: + return ( + "\n\n" + f"\n{city_block}\n" + "\n3\n\n" + "\n" + ) + + +def _stream(detector: Qwen3CoderDetector, text: str, chunk: int = 3) -> str: + args = "" + for i in range(0, len(text), chunk): + result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(text[i : i + chunk], TOOLS) + for item in result.calls: + args += item.parameters + return args + + +class TestQwen3CoderDetectorMalformedParameterEnd(CustomTestCase): + """A close marker the grammar let drift ("", "", + a bare "", "", "")) + self.assertEqual(json.loads(args), {"city": "Shanghai", "days": 3}) + + def test_well_formed_value_unchanged(self): + result = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse( + _call("Shanghai\n"), TOOLS + ) + self.assertEqual( + json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters), {"city": "Shanghai", "days": 3} + ) + + def test_angle_brackets_inside_value_are_kept(self): + result = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse( + _call("a tag city\n"), TOOLS + ) + self.assertEqual( + json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters)["city"], "a tag city" + ) + + def test_closed_value_ending_like_a_marker_is_kept(self): + """A value closed by a real may itself end in "" + or "" (e.g. XML a coder model writes); only an unclosed + value can carry a drifted marker.""" + for value in ("\n

1

\n", "x "): + with self.subTest(value=value): + text = _call(f"{value}\n") + parsed = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS) + self.assertEqual(json.loads(parsed.calls[0].parameters)["city"], value) + self.assertEqual( + json.loads(_stream(Qwen3CoderDetector(), text))["city"], value + ) + + def test_long_whitespace_run_in_unclosed_value_parses_in_linear_time(self): + """Finding a drifted marker at the end of an unclosed value must not rescan + from every whitespace position (quadratic on long whitespace runs).""" + value = "a" + " " * 100_000 + "b" + text = ( + "\n\n" + f"\n{value}\n" + "\n3\n\n" + "\n" + ) + start = time.perf_counter() + result = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS) + self.assertLess(time.perf_counter() - start, 2.0) + self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters)["city"], value) + + +if __name__ == "__main__": + import unittest + + unittest.main()
